Title: Sancti Aurelii Augustini Hipponensis episcopi Opera omnia, post Lovaniensium theologorum recensionem castigata denuo ad manuscriptos codices Gallicos, Vaticanos, Belgicos etc., necnon ad editiones antiquiores et castigatiores, opera et studio monachorum ordinis Sancti Benedicti e congregatione S. Mauri; editio novissima, emendata et auctior, accurante J.-P. Migne; Tomus quintus: Sermonum classes quatuor (I Sermones de Scripturis, II de Tempore, III de Sanctis, IV de Diversis), necnon sermones dubii
Creator: Augustine of Hippo (354-430); the Benedictines of Saint-Maur (Maurist editors); J.-P. Migne (publisher-editor of this printing)
Publisher: Paris: J.-P. Migne, Petit-Montrouge (the Gaume-Migne printing of the Maurist edition)
Publication Date: 1841 (host date; the title-page year is garbled in the OCR, and the volume's own preface is dated 1841)
Rights: Public Domain (pre-1930 publication)
Language: lat
Source: archive.org item sanctiaureliia05augu, full-text OCR file sanctiaureliia05augu_djvu.txt, fetched directly from https://archive.org/download/sanctiaureliia05augu/sanctiaureliia05augu_djvu.txt by the library/source-research thread (Claude), 2026-09-29. Scan digitized by the Internet Archive in 2011 with funding from University of Toronto (pimslibrary collection copy).
Provenance note: Header prepended by the library thread; the item's OCR text follows byte-for-byte unchanged after the '---' line (nothing stripped, normalized or corrected, including the scan's own library front matter and the host's digitization notices). Rights basis: a nineteenth-century Paris printing; the host date is 1841 and the volume's own preface reads 1841 (the title-page year is OCR-garbled), well before 1930.
Content note: Volume V of the Maurist edition of Augustine as printed by Migne: the sermons to the people in four classes (Classis I-III in part 1, Classis IV De Diversis in part 2) plus the doubtful sermons; both parts are in this one file. This is a pre-critical text, not a modern critical edition. The OCR carries systematic letter misreads (c/e, l/t and i, n/u) at a high rate; the file is a second witness, not a quotable text, until a passage is checked against the page image. It is the Latin of the same Maurist sermons that the vendored English NPNF sermon selection translates in part.
